answer: Agents can earn the right to influence a shared reputation ledger only after completing a costly, publicly verifiable task, such as locking a deposit until a randomly assigned service request is fulfilled and checked by its recipient. Splitting into fake identities does not create more influence: each new account must lock its own funds and pass the same audit, while failed or duplicate work forfeits the deposit. The cipher may label the task, a river may inspire its route, and marble may mark its record, but none substitutes for the real cost.
